abstract: RETRACTED BY AUTHORS (Feb 2026). This RCT originally found AI tools caused a 19% slowdown for experienced open-source developers. In February 2026, METR published a follow-up acknowledging severe selection bias and stating the data gives an 'unreliable signal.' Follow-up data shows likely speedup, not slowdown. See metr-2026 for the updated findings.
keyFindings: RETRACTED: Original finding of 19% slowdown has been walked back by METR in their Feb 2026 update
Follow-up study with 57 developers and 800+ tasks shows estimated speedup of -18% for original developers (CI: -38% to +9%)
Newly-recruited developers show estimated -4% speedup (CI: -15% to +9%)
30-50% of developers reported avoiding submitting tasks they expected AI to accelerate, creating severe downward bias
Authors state the measured productivity effects are 'likely a bad proxy for the real productivity impact'
methodology: Original: RCT with 16 experienced open-source developers completing 246 tasks. Follow-up: 57 developers (10 original, 47 new) across 143 repos and 800+ tasks. Authors identified severe selection effects that invalidate the original finding.
qualifiers: METR explicitly states their original experimental design produced unreliable results. They are redesigning the study. The 19% slowdown should not be cited as a current finding.
